introduction_section.heading: What is Enterprise Grade
content: Enterprise grade Robotic Process Automation uses software bots to perform repetitive, rule based tasks that humans normally complete through screens, forms, spreadsheets, emails, documents, portals, and legacy applications. RPA is useful when systems do not have clean APIs or when teams still rely on manual clicking, copying, downloading, uploading, and verification work.

At Devisgon, we build RPA solutions with workflow analysis, bot logic, OCR extraction, data validation, exception handling, secure credential management, monitoring dashboards, reporting, and long term maintenance. Our bots can process invoices, update records, download reports, move files, submit forms, reconcile data, and operate across older systems without forcing a full platform replacement.

RPA is especially valuable for finance, healthcare, logistics, insurance, HR, operations, customer support, and back office teams that need faster processing while keeping existing software infrastructure in place.
introduction_section.highlight_quote: “RPA turns repetitive screen based work into reliable digital operations that run faster, cleaner, and with stronger process control.”

faq_section.title: Robotic Process Automation Questions and Answers
faq_section.subtitle: Detailed answers for operations teams, finance leaders, CTOs, back office teams, and businesses planning RPA automation

questions.question: What is Robotic Process Automation?
questions.answer: Robotic Process Automation uses software bots to perform repetitive rule based tasks that humans normally complete through screens, forms, documents, spreadsheets, and business systems. RPA can copy data, submit forms, download reports, process documents, update records, and interact with older systems. It is useful when full API integration is not available or not practical.

questions.question: What business tasks can RPA automate?
questions.answer: RPA can automate invoice processing, data entry, report downloads, file movement, spreadsheet updates, vendor record checks, customer onboarding steps, HR workflows, claims processing, system reconciliation, and legacy software operations. The best RPA candidates are repetitive, rule based, high volume tasks with clear inputs and outputs.

questions.question: Can RPA automate invoice extraction?
questions.answer: Yes. RPA can combine OCR, document parsing, field extraction, validation rules, and approval workflows to automate invoice processing. Extracted values can be checked against vendor records, purchase orders, accounting rules, or internal systems. Exceptions can be routed to a human reviewer before final posting.

questions.question: Does RPA work with legacy systems?
questions.answer: Yes. RPA is often useful for legacy systems because bots can interact with interfaces the way users do. They can click buttons, fill forms, copy values, download files, and update records even when the application does not provide a modern API. This avoids forcing a full system replacement immediately.

questions.question: Is RPA secure?
questions.answer: RPA can be secure when bots use controlled credentials, role based permissions, encrypted storage, audit logs, monitoring, and approval boundaries. Bots should only access the systems and actions they are authorized to perform. Sensitive workflows require strong governance and exception handling.

questions.question: How is RPA different from API automation?
questions.answer: API automation connects systems directly through structured interfaces, while RPA automates user interface actions when APIs are unavailable, limited, or costly to implement. API automation is usually more stable when available, but RPA is valuable for older tools, desktop apps, portals, and manual screen based workflows.

questions.question: How long does an RPA project take?
questions.answer: The timeline depends on process complexity, number of systems, document formats, exception rules, bot logic, security requirements, and testing needs. A focused data entry or report automation can be delivered faster, while multi system invoice or legacy automation requires deeper mapping and validation.

questions.question: Does Devisgon provide RPA maintenance after deployment?
questions.answer: Yes. RPA bots need maintenance when screens change, fields move, document layouts vary, business rules change, or systems update. Devisgon provides monitoring, bug fixes, bot updates, accuracy improvements, exception review, workflow optimization, and ongoing RPA support.
